title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: actual past vs inhering vice — before four proofs
pass_a_gloss: Five millennia back Adam's first deed of sin is gone from the furniture of things; the vice that sticks with human nature is still alive and at work. One act then; as many inhering instances now as there are persons. Deed versus habit-shape; outside us and impossible to lodge in us versus inside and clinging; ours only if God reckons it versus ours because it truly inheres; fault on your telling versus penalty of that fault. Clear that fog, and ask what reasons force Romans 5's entered-sin to mean Adam's actual—Pighius's line, which even Bellarmine answered with several strokes. I will not blunt you with those prejudices here.
pass_b_english: Adam's first actual sin, committed some five thousand years ago, has passed, and did not remain in the nature of things: inhering vice remained with human nature, and is and thrives today. That is unique in number; of this there are as many individuals as there are humans. That was an action; this stands in the manner of a habit. That is outside us, and it is not possible for it to be in us; this is within us, sticking in us. That you think is ours, but only by God's imputation; this is truly ours, deeply inhering in us: That you will have as fault; this as its penalty. With this ambiguity and confusion removed, let us see by what reasons you prove that the Apostle by the sin which entered into the world understands Adam's actual sin. Which was certainly Pighius's opinion, which Bellarmine himself refuted with some arguments, but I do not wish to press you with prejudices.
source_text: Peccatum primum actuale Adami ante quinque millia annorum commissum praeteriit, nec permansit in rerum natura: vitium inhaerens cum natura humana permansit, estque & viget hodie. Illud unicum est numero, hujus tot sunt individua quot homines. Illud fuit actio, hoc se habet ad modum habitus. Illud extra nos est, nec possibile est esse in nobis, hoc est intra nos in nobis haerens. Illud tu putas nostrum esse, sed imputatione duntaxat Dei, hoc vere nostrum est, nobis penitus inhaerens: Illud vis esse culpam, hoc illius poenam. Hac ambiguitate & confusione sublata, videamus quibus rationibus probes, Apostolum per peccatum quod in mundum introiit peccatum actuale Adami intelligere. Quae certe fuit sententia Pighii, quam ipse Bellarminus aliquot argumentis confutavit, sed nolo te praejudiciis urgere.
